stages.label: Layout
stages.purpose: Establish camera, masses, negative space, threshold, and fixed-object regions before paint.

stages.label: Rough Key
stages.purpose: Make the whole image read through broad masses and gesture before detail.

stages.label: Breakdown
stages.purpose: Turn broad masses into volume, plane relationships, and spatial continuity.

stages.label: Eye Response 0001
stages.purpose: Test whether eight perception-led marks can create a believable wall/floor/threshold depth hinge before Second Key.

stages.label: Second Key
stages.purpose: Clarify object identity and form without flattening the rough-key gesture.

stages.label: Material / Light
stages.purpose: Let velvet, ember, wall, floor, and threshold acquire distinct material behavior.

stages.label: Cleanup
stages.purpose: Resolve only the edges and details that strengthen the image's read.

stages.label: Composite
stages.purpose: Balance glaze, atmosphere, hierarchy, and final integration without rewriting structure.

questions: At thumbnail scale, does the room read more as one spatial place than it did at the Breakdown checkpoint?
Does the threshold now behave more like recession and less like a dark vertical mark?
Do the floor cues lead the eye toward the threshold without becoming drawn perspective lines?
Did the upper-right wall become quieter and more architectural rather than merely blurrier?
Were fire, cushion, negative space, and scene asymmetry preserved without compensatory edits?
Which of the eight Eye Response marks had the highest perceptual leverage?
After this response, is the next bottleneck still perception, or is it now the expressive power of the Hand?
